hook: JNTUH cyber security: quantum cryptography only a *4th-year* elective
hook_b: JNTUH cyber security: quantum cryptography only a *4th-year* elective
tldr: Sakshi reports concerns that quantum computing in Telangana engineering colleges is limited to the syllabus, without dedicated labs or hands-on training.

beats.what: JNTUH's CSE (Cyber Security) syllabus lists quantum computing and quantum cryptography as electives in the first semester of the fourth year.
beats.why: First-year Advanced Engineering Physics introduces quantum computing basics, which experts quoted say is not enough for deeper skills.
beats.care: Students wanting practical work on qubits, quantum gates and post-quantum cryptography may find colleges lack labs and trained faculty, the report says.

causes.label: Quantum seen as future cyber security challenge

event.label: Syllabus has it only as late elective

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Experts quoted call for a field-level review of facilities in colleges.

cards.q: Should quantum topics be compulsory for cyber security students?

qs: Which skills do employers ask cyber security graduates for today?

facts.t: JNTUH's cyber security syllabus lists *2* quantum electives: quantum computing and quantum cryptography.

viz.l: Where quantum sits in the B.Tech
viz.verdict: Basics early, depth only as an option

learn.t: Post-quantum cryptography = encryption designed to stay safe against future quantum computers

watch: Whether JNTUH reviews lab facilities for quantum courses, as experts quoted suggest.
fact: JNTUH cyber security students meet quantum cryptography only as a *4th-year* elective
twist: Because it is an elective, there is no guarantee every cyber security student studies it at all.
